calibration_rulings.title: The Hours value 'Open 24 hours' (Arabic 'open round the clock (24 hours)'): its Urdu on the five pages of b5, and on the later pages that carry the same value (parks, a beach).
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban, kanzan, arbaa, thulaim, tuwaither: practical[1].value (unchanged from stage 1). Every later page whose source value is 'Open 24 hours'.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. TWO FIXED STRINGS for the one English value: «24 گھنٹے کھلا رہتا ہے» where the page's own name is masculine, «24 گھنٹے کھلی رہتی ہے» where it is feminine. HOW THE CHOICE IS MADE ON A LATER PAGE, without anyone's ear: by the gender field of the termbase entry of that page's own title — the key the title is byte for byte — which is the gender the page's verbs already agree with. The five pages of b5 have «جبل» titles whose entries are masculine: the first string, five times, equal by script. A page whose title's entry is feminine (for instance a title whose noun is «تفریح گاہ», feminine in the termbase) takes the second. Nothing else in the string varies: the figure stays a figure (the number check wants the English 24), «گھنٹے» follows it, and the value ends without a stop (ruling P26). The 24 is a length of time: neither string carries the clock word or a part of the day, so ruling P13 and build check C51 are not touched. The translation memory holds the masculine pair from this batch (five pairs, one string, no note); the feminine string stands in this ruling and enters the memory with the first feminine page; a later stage 1 chooses by the gender of the page's title entry, not by reusing the pair for its English. The value is carried into no other field, and no season, light or advice is added to it. On record for the owner, one line: B, «24 گھنٹے» alone, if he wants one string for every page; and that an Hours row on an unfenced hill, beside two rows that already say open and free, is the source's. ROUND 2: CONFIRMED, LOUDLY, BOTH STRINGS AS THEY STAND — «24 گھنٹے کھلا رہتا ہے» and «24 گھنٹے کھلی رہتی ہے» — on two readers of the masculine one; they bind the later park and beach pages. FOR WHOEVER APPLIES IT (proof pass, finding 20): on a later page the entry of the page's own title is, until that page's judge approves it, the proposal of its stage 1 — the gender is read from that entry and confirmed by that judge; and a pair of the translation memory has no field for a gender (its keys are en, ur, page, field, date, note), so a pair names its gender only where someone writes it in `note` (the five pairs of this batch carry none), and a tool that reuses a pair by its English alone does not choose between them: the translator of stage 1 does, by the rule above.
calibration_rulings.guard: The five cells of b5 are equal by script (the build script of this file compares them). For the proofreader, not machine-read: the value is one of the two strings byte for byte; its gender is that of the termbase entry of the page's title; the clock word of ruling P13 stands nowhere in it.

calibration_rulings.title: '100,000 square metres' (Arabic in words, 'a hundred thousand'): a figure of exactly one lakh, and a measure rather than a count.
calibration_rulings.binds: tuwaither::body: the form to be written there once the tools can pass it; until then the one recorded exception (the coordinator's decision of round 2). Every later figure of one lakh or more that the English gives in bare digits, count or measure (an area, a length, a capacity, a population).
calibration_rulings.ruling: THE LINE'S FORM IS A. A figure of one lakh or more is written in the Urdu scale, in digits with the scale word, whether it counts things or measures them, and the unit follows the scale word: «1 لاکھ مربع میٹر». This is ruling P10 applied, not a new rule: the scale 'begins at one lakh'; a measure is written like a count (the unit after the figure, ruling N24); the reference corpus writes areas of this size so; and each reader who met the digits converted them. Below one lakh nothing changes («10,000 مربع میٹر» on sahood stands). C stays refused: the figure is a figure. WHAT STANDS IN THE TEXT (in round 1, and in round 2 by the decision recorded below), and why: «100,000 مربع میٹر» (tuwaither, body), the source's digits grouped as the English groups them — for one reason only, the limit of the stage checker stated above. The value is the same in both forms and no fact turns on the choice. THE DECISION IS THE COORDINATOR'S, one of two, and this entry is true under either: (1) the checker is taught to compare a bare source figure of one lakh or more with a scaled Urdu figure by value, and the string «100,000 مربع میٹر» is replaced by «1 لاکھ مربع میٹر» in tuwaither::body — one replacement, the rest of the sentence unchanged («… کہ 1 لاکھ مربع میٹر کے رقبے پر اس پہاڑ کو …»); or (2) the digits stay as a recorded exception of this one string until then. Until (1) is done the page is charged one point under compliance and the first reader's conversion under fit. ROUND 2 — THE COORDINATOR HAS DECIDED: (2). The text keeps «100,000 مربع میٹر» in round 2 as the RECORDED EXCEPTION of this one string: the stage checker and the build's number guard cannot yet pass a lakh form for a bare figure; teaching them is tooling work for a later round, after which this one string is replaced by «1 لاکھ مربع میٹر». THE RULING STANDS AS WORDED: the line's form is A. Wherever this item is cited, the exception is cited with it — no citation of N66-a-round-lakh-and-a-measure means that the ruling writes the digits. The point under compliance stays charged on tuwaither, and both readers' conversion under fit, until the string is replaced.
calibration_rulings.guard: Not machine-enforced today, and the stage checker would refuse the ruled form: that limit, and the coordinator's decision of round 2 that follows from it, are the reason the text differs from the ruling. For the proofreader, not machine-read: a figure of one lakh or more written in bare digits is reported with this item's id; in this batch there is one, in tuwaither::body, and it is the recorded exception.

calibration_rulings.title: The kicker of a page whose only kicker source is the Arabic «معلم طبيعي» (no English kicker; not rendered today).
calibration_rulings.binds: The five kickers of b5, equal by script. Every later page with that Arabic kicker.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «قدرتی مقام», one string on the five pages and on every later page whose Arabic kicker is «معلم طبيعي». No final stop, no gloss. It stands in no sentence with the largest-oasis claim (C15).
calibration_rulings.guard: The five kickers are equal by script. For the proofreader, not machine-read: a page whose Arabic kicker is this one carries this string byte for byte.

calibration_rulings.title: Al-Ahsa Municipality (Arabic «أمانة الأحساء»): the Urdu name of the body.
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan::body, arbaa::body, tuwaither::body. Every later page that names the municipality.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: «الاحساء کی بلدیہ», feminine («بنا رہی ہے»; with «نے» the verb agrees with its object), no quotation marks, inflected like any phrase. It is ruling N44-royal-commission-name's build with a common Urdu noun. C is refused by the owner's rule on loans as it stands; B is on record for search. The entry stays pending for one reason: nothing in Urdu attests a wording for this body, and the Gulf's Urdu paper could not be read.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the body is named with the Urdu possessive and the noun «بلدیہ», carries no quotation marks, and takes feminine agreement.

calibration_rulings.title: Two Arabic nouns, a park («منتزه», kanzan) and a resort («منتجع», tuwaither): one Urdu noun or two?
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan::body, tuwaither::body. Every later page that names a resort.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. One Urdu noun whose dictionary senses cover both: a park is «تفریح گاہ», and a resort is said as «سیاحتی تفریح گاہ» with what it offers named in the same sentence. The loan stays out (ruling P16); B's nouns say a tourist site, which the mountain already is.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the resort carries the adjective «سیاحتی» before the noun, and the noun is the termbase key.

calibration_rulings.title: A «جبل» name whose meaning the source itself gives, inside a sentence and for the second word only ("earned its name ('the Four')", "the name — 'the sated one' —"): ruling P3c, case (c), asks for a bracket at the first mention; ruling P3a forbids a bracket after a «جبل» name.
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban::body, arbaa::body. Every later «جبل» page whose source glosses the name.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Ruling P3a governs a «جبل» name: no bracket, in title or body. A meaning the source gives in a sentence is given in that sentence, in the source's place, with the meaning word inside quotation marks as a word cited (ruling N16, point 5). Case (c) of ruling P3c does not reach a name whose generic ruling P3a keeps bare; the guards of P3a and P3c stay as they are. No meaning is supplied where no source gives one («ابا الکباری», «ابو حصیص», «الثلیم», «کنزان»).
calibration_rulings.guard: The machine-read guards of rulings P3a and P3c as they are. For the proofreader, not machine-read: on a «جبل» page the meaning of the name, if the source gives one, stands once, in a sentence, in quotation marks.

calibration_rulings.title: An editorial gloss that the English sets in square brackets inside a quotation ("'a mountain in Bahrain [the historic eastern coastlands], in whose caves one seeks the cool'"), and that the Arabic does not carry.
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban::body. Every later quotation in which the source sets a gloss of its own.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, as a change of form under ruling P23: an editorial gloss that the source sets inside a quotation stands in the Urdu as a sentence of the page's own, straight after the quotation, opening «یہاں … سے مراد», with the content of the bracket and no more. The defect is logged (an editorial gloss inside a quotation, English only; a gloss that does not say of which land), and B is on record as the literal wording. Nothing is added to say whose coast it is.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: nothing stands inside the quotation marks that the Arabic quotation lacks, and no square bracket stands in an Urdu string.

calibration_rulings.title: A second name of a place that both sources set in quotation marks and that carries no Urdu generic ('Aba Al-Kabari').
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban::summary, shaban::body (changes 0 and 1 of round 1). Every later second name of this kind. ROUND 2: shaban::body, the fourth mention of the bare cited name (round 2's change 1).
calibration_rulings.ruling: B. A second name that the source itself sets in quotation marks and that carries no Urdu generic stands inside U+201C and U+201D at every mention: «“ابا الکباری”». It is one more place for quotation marks beside those the line already has — the three of ruling N16, point 5 (an Arabic phrase kept as a name, a word cited as a word, the short name of a programme) and the translated byname of item N40-quoted-translated-byname; the meaning word of item N70-meaning-of-a-jabal-name-given-in-a-sentence is a word cited as a word, and a quotation proper needs no place of its own. A second name that carries an Urdu generic stays bare, as the approved pages have it. No gloss and no vowel sign: no source says what the name means or how it is vowelled (ruling P17), and that he cannot say it aloud is recorded in the entry. ROUND 2: confirmed for the second name. HOW THE PAGE'S OTHER CITED NAMES STAND, so that the page agrees with its own rule: a BARE name CITED AS A NAME — the name without its generic, spoken of as a name — stands in marks at every mention: «“الشبعان”» four times (the summary; the body three times, the third, «“الشبعان” کا نام اس پڑوسی ٹیلے کا ہو کر رہ گیا», since round 2's change 1) and «“القارہ”» once. A name IN USE, with its generic, stands bare («جبل الشبعان», «جبل القارہ»), as ruling P3a and every approved page have a «جبل» name. Round 1's change log said 'at every mention' while one mention stood bare, after the sources, which quote 'Al-Qarah' and not 'Al-Shaban' in that sentence; the statement is true of the text since round 2.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker, this clause, read from this file by R/tools/lib/rulings.mjs: the key «ابا الکباری» in the direct case stands between U+201C and U+201D. For the proofreader, not machine-read: a second name with an Urdu generic carries no marks. Also for the proofreader: on a page that sets a bare name in marks as a cited name, every citing mention of that name on that page stands in marks; a name cited once as a name on a page that marks it nowhere (kanzan's summary) is not ruled here; a name written with its generic stands bare.

calibration_rulings.title: The generic for a town (Arabic «بلدة», 'the town of Al-Taraf'): the word, and its place before or after the name.
calibration_rulings.binds: arbaa::body, arbaa::area (changes 9 and 11 of round 1; round 2's changes 5 and 6). Point (1): every later page that names a town with its generic. Point (2): every later mention of Al-Taraf, and any later name that a stage raises as a homograph of a common Urdu word.
calibration_rulings.ruling: ROUND 2: C FOR THIS TOWN, AND THE ORDER OF B FOR EVERY TOWN. Round 1 ruled two things in one sentence; they are told apart here. (1) THE ORDER, for every town: a town is «قصبہ», masculine, and its generic stands AFTER the name, as the round writes «گاؤں» and «شہر»; after a name it inflects like any noun (oblique singular and direct plural «قصبے»). NOT REOPENED: «محلہ» stands before its name, as the approved pages of round 1, b3 and b4 and rulings N45-quarter-inside-a-district, N61-district-generic-in-a-summary and N63-district-name-with-a-translated-direction have it («محلہ الکوت», «محلہ القوع»). (2) THE HOMOGRAPH, which is the case of «الطرف» alone today: the bare name is the Urdu «طرف» with an article, and NEITHER ORDER FENCES IT. The first reader read A as 'the town on the side'; the second read B as a garbled 'towards the town in the north'. Round 1 moved the generic to cure exactly this and did not cure it. Both readers offered the same third form, the first as «الطرف نامی قصبہ», the second as «الطرف نام کا قصبہ»; round 1 had put it on record as the fallback 'if a later reader trips on B'. It is the line's own form for a name the reader cannot take for a name on sight — «سوق القیصریہ نامی بازار» (ruling P3c, point 2), «الرویضہ نامی حصے» (b3, in its body and in its area line). This town is written so at every mention, in body and card: «الطرف نامی قصبہ», «الطرف نامی قصبے کے قریب». The word between says that what stands before it is a name, and adds no fact; the order of point (1) is kept, which is also the order that agrees with the site's «X گاؤں». SCOPE (proof pass, finding 5): point (2) is the rule of «الطرف» and of any later place whose bare name spells a common Urdu word — raised as its own case by the stage that meets it; a town whose name is no such homograph takes the plain order of point (1). WHERE THE SOURCES ARE BARE: the generic is written where at least one of a field's two sources has it (arbaa's area line: the Arabic has it, the English lacks it). Where BOTH sources of a field name a town bare, the case is RAISED to the judge of that page and not completed silently — the fence of items N61-district-generic-in-a-summary and N77-bare-settlement-name-al-qarah; for «الطرف» the homograph is then that judge's ground for completing it, stated in the record. In b5 no field names the town bare in both sources. RECORDED for whoever may reopen the quarter's word: the first reader says the place word stands before one kind of name and after the others, and neither reader of this batch can picture a mountain in a «محلہ».
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the word for a town stands after the name it belongs to, inflected before a postposition; the town Al-Taraf has the word that marks a name between its name and its generic at every mention; the word for a quarter stands before its name, uninflected; a town named bare in both sources of a field is raised, not given a generic silently.

calibration_rulings.title: thulaim's area line: English 'West of Al-Oyoun — north of Al-Ahsa', Arabic «غرب مدينة العيون — شمال الأحساء»; the page's own text puts the mountain at Al-Ahsa's northern entrance.
calibration_rulings.binds: thulaim::area. Any later area line whose English can be read as outside the region its page places it in.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Where the English and the Arabic of an area line differ on a fact, the Arabic is the authority: the mountain is in the north of Al-Ahsa, «الاحساء کے شمالی حصے میں». The line keeps the source's order and ends in a postposition (ruling N30-area-line-without-a-larger-bare-place); C would drop the source's second position. The English wording is logged as a defect of the source, and B is on record as the literal wording.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the line says a part of Al-Ahsa, not a direction from it.

calibration_rulings.title: 'The northern oasis' (Arabic «الواحة الشمالية»): a term the source uses as known and explains on no page.
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan::body (change 4 of round 1). Every later page that speaks of the northern or the eastern oasis.
calibration_rulings.ruling: C. The source's term is kept and takes the name at its mention: «الاحساء کے شمالی نخلستان». The owner's name is set before the source's term by this item; ruling N47-the-oasis-on-a-page-that-has-not-named-it's own form is «الاحساء کے نخلستان» with nothing between, and its guard is met on kanzan by the summary alone (proof pass, finding 9). No fact enters. B is not taken: it turns a term of the source into a description and says of the northern oasis that it is a part of the oasis, which this page's source does not say in so many words; it is on record for the owner as the reading that would make one picture of summary and body. The difference between the two fields is the source's and is logged. ROUND 2: C was read by the second reader (his item 23, minor; the first reader's item on the bare term was moderate): 'the second makes me think there is a separate northern oasis'. The doubt is smaller and is still there, and it is the source's on both counts — a term used as known and explained nowhere, and two placements of the massif in two fields. C STANDS; B stays the owner's option.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the term stands with «الاحساء کے» before it at its first mention on a page.

calibration_rulings.title: A list of villages ('the villages of Al-Shu'bah, Al-Kilabiyah, Al-Battaliyah and Al-Jurn'): the generic after each name, as the entries of two of them say, or once?
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan::body, kanzan::area. Every later list of villages, towns or quarters.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. In a list of villages the generic stands once, after the last name, and the plural verb shows the number («… اور الجرن گاؤں اس کے پڑوس میں ہیں»). The entries of «الکلابیہ» and «البطالیہ», which this file does not re-enter, take one line from the coordinator: in a list the generic stands once, after the last name.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a list of two or more villages carries one generic, after the last name.

calibration_rulings.title: The settlement Al-Qarah named bare in both sources ('the palm groves of Al-Tuwaither and Al-Qarah'): the bare word is the second word of the calibrated key «جبل القارہ».
calibration_rulings.binds: tuwaither::body. Every later page that names the settlement.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. The settlement stands bare where both sources have it bare (the fence read field by field, item N61-district-generic-in-a-summary); the mountain's key is never written for the settlement, and the settlement's name is given no other spelling than the key's second word. B is the owner's option if the source gains the word. ROUND 2: A stands, on the fence of item N61-district-generic-in-a-summary (no generic where both sources of the field are bare); the second reader's remark is logged as the source's, and B remains the owner's option.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: where «القارہ» stands without «جبل» before it, its source names the settlement or cites the name as a name.

calibration_rulings.title: 'His brother Prince Saad fell' (Arabic 'was martyred'): the Urdu verb for a death in battle of a person the page honours.
calibration_rulings.binds: kanzan::body (change 6 of round 1, reversed by round 2's change 4). Every later sentence of this kind.
calibration_rulings.ruling: ROUND 2: A. ROUND 1's D IS WITHDRAWN, loudly. Of a person the page names with honour, a death in battle that the English tells with 'fell' is «مارے گئے», in the honorific plural: the plain Urdu for one killed in battle, which says what the English says. WHY THE RULING TURNS: round 1 chose D on one reader and wrote that 'the next blind reader is its test'. The second reader hears D as 'what the news says about accident victims; for a man killed in battle it sounds off' and gives A as the wording that works; the proof pass finds D said 'rarely of one who falls fighting'; the reference counts read at stage 4 and in round 1 go the same way (see the evidence). On register the two readers are one against one — the first found A 'blunt for a prince of a Muslim royal house' — so register does not decide; meaning and usage do. A's cost is on record: to one reader of two it is blunt. B stays withdrawn for the reason stage 4 gave. C, the Arabic's word, is not adopted — the English is the translation source and says 'fell', and the German, Russian and Chinese lines follow it — and stays the owner's option, one line, and the one wording both readers would accept: «ان کے بھائی شہزادہ سعد شہید ہوئے». D stays on record as the wording the first reader expected. A later judge who meets a reader faulting A has this record of both readers, not a fresh choice between A and D.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the verb is in the honorific plural and no benediction follows the name.

calibration_rulings.title: 'A project to humanise the Jabal Al-Arba road' (Arabic «مشروعاً لأنسنة طريق جبل الأربع»): a term of town planning that neither source explains.
calibration_rulings.binds: arbaa::body (change 10 of round 1). Every later page that reports a project to 'humanise' a street, a road or a quarter.
calibration_rulings.ruling: D. The planning term is said in plain words: the verb Urdu uses of a road, «بہتر بنانا», with the one thing the term says, for whom — «لوگوں کے لیے». A is withdrawn: its adjective is said of surroundings, not of a road, and failed the first reader. B is not taken: of a road it reads as a mistranslation; it stays on record as the literal. C drops what the term says. Nothing is added about the works (no surface, pavement, lighting or date) or about how the place is reached today; the project is launched, not finished. ROUND 2: D STANDS. The second reader read it (his item 28, moderate, of which he calls the missing access 'more important'): 'vague and sounds translated'. Better than A, which the first reader could not take as Urdu at all, and not cured. The vagueness is the source's: a planning term neither language explains. A plainer wording exists — C — and is not taken, because it drops the one thing the term says, for whom, and the content of a field's source is not traded for a better register, whatever the number of readers (rulings P24 and P25). C is the owner's option, one line: «سڑک کو بہتر بنانے کا ایک منصوبہ». D's cost is charged under nativeness. D still has no count behind it.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the sentence names no work done to the road and no date.

calibration_rulings.title: An impersonal verb inside a quotation ('in whose caves one seeks the cool', Arabic «يتبرّد بكهافه»): the Urdu passive, or «لوگ» with an active verb?
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban::body. Every later quotation with an impersonal verb.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Inside a quotation as outside it, the source's impersonal subject is «لوگ» with the active verb; it renders 'one' and is not a word added to the quotation. No season, time of day or warmth enters with it (C16 untouched).
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: nothing inside the marks goes beyond the Arabic quotation.

calibration_rulings.title: shaban's summary: "also called 'Aba Al-Kabari'; the old sources applied its name to Al-Qarah Mountain" — the pronoun follows the second name and does not say which name is meant, in both languages.
calibration_rulings.binds: shaban::summary.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A, under ruling P23: where a summary's pronoun follows a second name and could be taken for it, the name meant is said outright, in the body's own words and in quotation marks as a name cited as a name. No fact new to the page enters. The defect is logged and B is on record as the literal wording. ROUND 2: A stands; the second reader's remark is logged as the source's. The rule for the marks of a bare cited name is stated in item N72-marks-round-a-second-name-the-source-quotes.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: the summary names the same name the body names.

calibration_rulings.title: A transliterated name whose Arabic spelling ends in alif maqsura («سلوى», Salwa): the letterform guard rejects U+0649, and the line had no rule for what is written in its place.
calibration_rulings.binds: arbaa::body (change 7 of round 1; unchanged in round 2). Every later transliterated name whose Arabic ends in alif maqsura: first «الموسیٰ» (musa-park) and «سلویٰ» (salwa-beach). Not the month «جمادی الاول»; not Urdu dictionary words.
calibration_rulings.ruling: B, as ruled in round 1; REWORDED in round 2 (proof pass, finding 4) so that the ruling, its ground and its guard say one thing. WHAT IS RULED: a transliterated NAME — a name the line builds letter for letter from its Arabic spelling — whose Arabic ends in alif maqsura (ى) is written with «ی» (U+06CC) followed by the superscript alif (U+0670): «سلویٰ». THE GROUND is the identity of the letter, not a count of spellings: Arabic ى and ي are two letters; the letterform guard rejects both Arabic code points; Urdu writes the second «ی» and has «یٰ» for the first, so that without the mark the name is spelled as if its Arabic ended in ya — another name (the first reader read 'salvi'). The mark therefore belongs to the spelling of the name and is not a vowel sign added to help pronunciation: ruling P17, and the reading of it in open item N7, are untouched, and no zabar, zer, pesh or jazm is written on any name. The reference counts in the evidence show that Urdu usage writes such names both ways; they are why the unmarked form is on record for the owner, not the ground of the ruling. WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE: Urdu words whose dictionary spelling carries the mark («اعلیٰ», «دعویٰ», «حتیٰ», «ادنیٰ»). None stands on the site today; the page that first needs one writes it as the dictionary does, and it is no finding under this item. A name with a settled Urdu form of its own keeps that form: the applied «جمادی الاول» is the Urdu name of a month, keyed with its own reference title, not a name transliterated letter for letter, and it is NOT changed by this ruling. WHAT IT BINDS NEXT: «الموسیٰ» for the Arabic «الموسى» in the title of musa-park, and «سلویٰ» again in the title of salwa-beach — each written with the mark from its stage 1 on. The key «سلوی» stays retired for «سلویٰ». On record for the owner, one line: A, the unmarked spelling, which is what the reference site's title for the Kuwaiti place of the same name has.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: the retired key is read from this entry by R/tools/lib/rulings.mjs, and the unmarked word standing whole in a text of the attraction batches is then a finding; the marked word is not, the mark being a combining sign the checker counts with the word. For the proofreader, not machine-read: in a transliterated name built from its Arabic spelling, U+0670 stands only after a final U+06CC whose Arabic letter is alif maqsura, and such a name is never written with the bare final letter; an Urdu word whose dictionary spelling carries the mark is not ruled here and is not a finding. Not the month named in the binds, which keeps its settled Urdu form.

calibration_rulings.title: The order of an area line whose source names no larger place as a bare name ('Al-Battaliyah village — northeast of Hofuf', 'Al-Koot district — central Hofuf').
calibration_rulings.binds: jalaniyah::area, unchanged. BINDS b4: hubaish «محلہ جنوبی الرفعہ، ہفوف کے وسط میں», umzurainiq «محلہ العویمریہ، ہفوف کے وسط میں» and uqair-mosque's area line keep the source's order as they stand. Round 1's six lines (al-uqair, jawatha-mosque, ameeriah, khuzam, baiah, uqair-castle) stand unchanged. Every later area line of the pattern. ROUND 2: unchanged for both batches.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A. Where the source's area line names no larger place as a bare name — it gives a village, a quarter or a port and then where that lies by a direction or a part of the town — the Urdu keeps the source's order: the place with its generic, then «،», then the position, which ends in a postposition: «البطالیہ گاؤں، ہفوف کے شمال مشرق میں», «محلہ الکوت، ہفوف کے وسط میں». Ruling P20 is untouched and holds wherever the source names a larger place as a bare name: that place leads («ہفوف، محلہ الکوت»; «الاحساء، مشرقی دیہات میں التہیمیہ گاؤں»). The two orders are therefore two cases of one rule — what the source gives as a bare larger name leads, and what it gives as a position follows — and no line of round 1 moves. Cost, stated: the same quarter can still stand quarter-first on one page and town-first on another where its sources word the line differently; that is logged with the sources' defects and is the owner's to even out in the source. On record for him, one line: B for every such line («ہفوف کے شمال مشرق میں، البطالیہ گاؤں»), which would move ten lines on applied pages. ‖ b4, ROUND 1: adopted as b3's judge ruled it; nothing moves. hubaish::area and umzurainiq::area keep the source's order and end in a postposition; uqair-mosque::area is the approved line of uqair-castle from the translation memory, which also ends in one; tahimiyah-e and abubakr-mosque lead with the larger bare place (ruling P20). b4's first reader read the five rows and remarked, as a minor item, that the row is built four different ways and that he had to re-orient each time (observation 7): the two cases of this rule over four wordings of the sources, logged with the sources' defects as this entry says. The checker's three notes of ruling P20 on b4 are these three lines and are expected. b4, ROUND 2: unchanged. The second reader of b4 (his item 47, minor) notes that abubakr-mosque's row puts the town first where hubaish and umzurainiq put the quarter first: the two cases of this rule over the sources' wordings, logged as before. The checker's three notes of ruling P20 are still these three lines. ‖ b5, ROUND 1: adopted and applied on four lines. The sources of shaban, kanzan, arbaa and thulaim give two positions and name no larger place as a bare name, so each line keeps the source's order and ends in a postposition: «التویثیر کے قریب، ہفوف کے مشرق میں», «ہفوف کے شمال مشرق میں، الشعبہ اور الکلابیہ گاؤں کے قریب», «ہفوف کے جنوب مشرق میں، الطرف نامی قصبے کے قریب», «العیون شہر کے مغرب میں، الاحساء کے شمالی حصے میں». tuwaither's source names the larger place bare and its line leads with it (ruling P20): «الاحساء، مشرقی دیہات میں التویثیر گاؤں», the approved build of both tahimiyah lines. The stage checker's four notes of ruling P20 on b5 are these four lines and are expected. In round 1 arbaa's line changed only in the place of the town's generic (item N73-generic-for-a-town); what thulaim's second position says is item N74-area-line-north-of-al-ahsa. The first reader (his item 42, moderate) notes that tuwaither's row is built differently from the other four: the two cases of this rule over the sources' wordings, logged as before. ROUND 2: arbaa's line changed again by one word, «نامی», between the town's name and its generic (item N73-generic-for-a-town as amended; round 2's change 6); it keeps the source's order and ends in a postposition. The other four lines are round 1's. The second reader, too, notes that tuwaither's row is built differently from the other four (his item 38): the two cases of this rule over the sources' wordings.
calibration_rulings.guard: Stage checker: its note of ruling P20 on an area line of this pattern is expected and is not a finding. For the proofreader, not machine-read: an area line that does not open with a bare larger place has a source that names none, and ends in a postposition, never in a bare place name after the comma.

calibration_rulings.title: 'The oasis' on a page whose text nowhere names the oasis ('the depth of learning in the oasis', 'an entire era of the oasis's history').
calibration_rulings.binds: bubakr-ribat::body, qubba-mosque::body: both leaves were changed in b3's round 2 (its changes 2, 3 and 5), and the sentence of the oasis in each is unchanged. b4: no string of its present text has the word for an oasis; the ruling binds b4, and every later page, only where a page mentions the oasis and no field of it names it. The calibration page and the pages of round 1: not bound as text, and not failed.
calibration_rulings.ruling: C, with the scope the evidence supports. A page that mentions the oasis names it at least once in its own text, in the form rulings P8 and N16 give: «الاحساء کے نخلستان», in the direct case «الاحساء کا نخلستان». Where a source says 'the oasis' on a page no field of which names it, the Urdu names it at that mention: so on bubakr-ribat and qubba-mosque. On a page that does name the oasis, the bare noun and the noun with a demonstrative may stand elsewhere. The ruling is NOT a rule about the first mention and NOT a rule about a summary read on its own: the calibration page (bare noun in the summary, the name at the opening of the body) is neither changed nor failed by it, and no page of round 1 is. B is not taken: it drops the source's noun. No fact enters: the oasis the source means is named, as its article names it. Cost, stated: on qubba-mosque the name lengthens a chain of possessives to four (charged under nativeness on that page). ‖ b5, ROUND 1: met on two pages and applied. kanzan mentions the oasis in summary and body and its source names it in neither: the summary names it, «الاحساء کے نخلستان کے شمال مشرق میں», and since round 1 the body's mention carries the name too, «الاحساء کے شمالی نخلستان کے مشرقی کنارے پر» (change 4 of round 1; item N75-the-northern-oasis). thulaim's source mentions the oasis three times in the body and names it nowhere: the Urdu names it at the first of them, «شمال سے الاحساء کے نخلستان میں آنے والے مسافروں», and the two later mentions stand as the bare noun. shaban, arbaa and tuwaither have no word for an oasis. The first reader made no remark on the antecedent of the word on either page. ROUND 2: unchanged on both pages. The body's wording on kanzan is item N75-the-northern-oasis's own (the name set before the source's term); this ruling's form is the summary's, which alone meets its guard there. The second reader made no remark on the antecedent of the word either; his doubt of two oases (his item 23) is item N75-the-northern-oasis's.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: a page of round 2 or later whose text has the word for an oasis has «الاحساء کے نخلستان» or «الاحساء کا نخلستان» in at least one of its fields. This is no test of which mention comes first and no test of a summary taken alone; a check written from it passes the calibration page as it stands.

calibration_rulings.title: The rider of ruling N14 (the page's name does not stand directly against another proper name in the opening sentence), which the ruling words for the fort pages: does it hold for a mosque page?
calibration_rulings.binds: hubaish::body, abubakr-mosque::body (the first sentence of each). b3: nothing moves — jalaniyah and bubakr-ribat open with the place, dibs has an adjective and qubba-mosque a bracket between the two names. Every later page.
calibration_rulings.ruling: A: CONFIRMED. The rider is not a rule about forts: on any attraction page, where the opening sentence would set the page's own name directly against another proper name, either the place comes first or a comma follows the name; the judge of the page chooses. On hubaish and abubakr-mosque the comma stands, as on khuzam and muhairis. It is not owed where a common noun, an adjective or a bracket already stands between the two names — umzurainiq («مسجد ام زرینیق محلہ العویمریہ میں واقع ہے») and, in b3, dibs and qubba-mosque — and it is not owed where the place comes first. SCOPE (round 2): 'another proper name' is a name a reader can run together with the page's name — of a town, a quarter, a village, a person, a family or a building. A common noun that serves as a name and is written bare like any noun («خلیج», ruling P5) is not such a name: «قلعہ العقیر خلیج کے ساحل پر، …» on the applied uqair-castle page is neither changed nor failed by this rule, and no page of round 1 is. uqair-mosque's opening carries no page name at all since round 2 («یہ تاریخی مسجد خلیج کے ساحل پر، …»). ‖ b5, ROUND 1: met on tuwaither and applied with the rule's other remedy. Stages 1 to 5 had the comma after the name, «جبل ابو حصیص، التویثیر گاؤں کے شمال میں، محلہ القوع میں کھڑا ہے۔»; the first reader (his item 41, moderate) calls a comma straight after the subject 'not Urdu punctuation'. The judge of the page chooses the place first: «التویثیر گاؤں کے شمال میں، محلہ القوع میں، جبل ابو حصیص کھڑا ہے۔» (change 18 of round 1). kanzan, arbaa and thulaim open with the place; shaban opens with a clause of its own («آج جس پہاڑ کو جبل الشبعان کہتے ہیں، وہ …»). No opening of b5 sets the page's name directly against another proper name. RECORDED for the rule: on hubaish and abubakr-mosque two readers passed the comma after the name without a remark; here one reader faulted it. Both remedies stay open to the judge of a page. ROUND 2: confirmed. The second reader read the place-first opening and made no remark on its punctuation or its order; what neither reader can picture is a mountain in a quarter north of a village (his item 38), the source's statement in the round's word for the quarter.
calibration_rulings.guard: For the proofreader, not machine-read: in the opening sentence of a body the page's title is never followed directly by the name of a town, a quarter, a village, a person, a family or a building. A common noun used as a name («خلیج») is not such a name. A check written from this passes every applied page as it stands, uqair-castle included. Two things such a check takes from the ruling: a generic that stands before the next name («محلہ العویمریہ») is the common noun between and not part of that name; and the rule is about the page's own title only: a place that is not the page, set against another name with only its generic between (the village in the openings of the two tahimiyah pages), is outside it.

open_items.title: A quoted Arabic word that is letter for letter an Urdu word («حسی», the singular of the name, reads as the adjective 'sensory'): how is the reader told what he is looking at?
open_items.provisional: Not settled: stays open. C is withdrawn — tried, read, no cure, and a word neither source carries; the conditions under which round 2 let it in (P23: the repaired text passes a blind read) were not met. The text stands in the wording of round 1, «لفظ “الاحساء”، “حسی” کی جمع ہے، یعنی …»: the order the first reader asked for and the second read without remark on the order. The homograph remains and is charged under fit. B, the remedy three readers ask for and the form the Arabic source itself uses, is barred by the P8 build guard (U+0650) and by ruling P17 as they stand, and a judge does not reopen a ruling. Recorded for whoever may: the build guard already exempts a termbase key that carries the sign (tools/check-ur-text.mjs, the registered-key exemption of P8), so the vocalised word would need an entry whose key carries the kasra and the sukun, the stage checker to honour the same exemption for a key the chain proposes, and the two signs in the Nastaliq subset.
